mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW M47D20 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned M47D20 supply-only costs £1,500-£3,200, with fitted prices from £2,200-£3,900 depending on labour and your location [EM-QUOTE]. Used engines start from around £400 but carry higher risk. Rebuilt units with upgraded components cost £2,500-£4,500 supply-only.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common failure on the M47D20 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Timing chain stretch and tensioner wear is the most common serious failure, typically appearing from 120,000 km (75,000 miles) upwards. Symptoms include metallic rattling on cold start and rough idling. Chain replacement costs £650-£1,800 if caught early. Swirl flap failure (M47TU) and turbo failure are also common.

mainEntity.name: Which BMW models use the M47D20 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M47D20 was fitted across BMW's range from 1998 to 2007. 1 Series (E81/E87): 118d, 120d. 3 Series (E46, E90): 318d, 320d. 5 Series (E39, E60): 520d. X3 (E83): 2.0d.

mainEntity.name: Should I buy a used or reconditioned M47D20 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned M47D20 is usually the better investment as it addresses known weak points including the timing chain, turbo and EGR system. Used engines are cheaper (£400+) but you inherit unknown condition. Reconditioned units (£1,500+) come with 12-24 month warranty. For E46 hosts under £3,000, evaluate scrap value before committing.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between M47D20, M47TU and M47TU2?

acceptedAnswer.text: The three generations differ primarily by fuel system and displacement. M47D20 (1998-2001): 1,951 cc, direct injection (Bosch VP44 pump), 136 hp. M47TU (2001-2004): 1,995 cc, common-rail, 150 hp, swirl flap failure risk. M47TU2 (2004-2007): 1,995 cc, common-rail, up to 163 hp, revised swirl flaps.

mainEntity.name: Is the M47D20 a reliable engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M47D20 is considered one of BMW's more durable diesel engines when properly maintained. Regular oil changes (every 10,000 miles or annually) are critical. The M47TU2 (2004+) is the most reliable variant. Preventative swirl flap deletion and timing chain inspection at 100k miles are recommended.

failures.title: BMW M47D20 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Wear
items.onset: 120,000-250,000 km (75,000-155,000 miles) if maintenance is neglected
items.whatHappens: The M47's timing chain is located at the rear of the engine, requiring engine removal for access. Chain stretch leads to metallic rattling noises on cold start, rough idling and misfires. In worst cases, the chain can jump teeth or break, causing catastrophic engine damage. The issue is made worse by poor maintenance and extended oil change intervals.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, a chain and tensioner replacement (£650-£1,800) can save the engine. If the chain has jumped or snapped, full engine replacement is usually the only viable option.

items.title: Swirl Flap Failure
items.whatHappens: The swirl flaps in the intake manifold can break or have their retaining screws work loose, entering the combustion chamber and destroying the engine. The M47TUD20 is the most affected variant; the M47TU2D20 received a revised design in 2004. Symptoms include rattling from the intake manifold area and reduced pulling power.
items.repairVsReplace: Swirl flap deletion with blanking plates is a common preventative modification. If a flap has already failed and entered the engine, replacement is often required.

items.title: Turbocharger Failure
items.whatHappens: Turbo failures on the M47 are common due to oil starvation, carbon build-up, or EGR-related issues. Signs include black or blue exhaust smoke, excessive oil consumption, turbo noise and loss of power. The M47D20TU has a reputation as a turbine destroyer due to overboost from blocked or misrouted EGR vacuum lines.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbo rebuild or replacement typically costs £600-£1,500. If the turbo has failed catastrophically and sent debris through the engine, full engine replacement may be required.

failures.goodYearsLine: The M47TU2 (2004 onwards) received improvements including a revised swirl flap design and common-rail injection, making it generally more reliable than earlier M47D20 and M47TUD20 units.

variants.title: M47D20 Sub-Codes Explained - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: The M47D20 name covers three distinct generations of BMW's 2.0-litre diesel. The differences matter - fitting the wrong revision can mean incompatible engine mounts, turbo plumbing, ECU calibration, or wiring looms.

relatives.description: 1998-2001 original direct-injection version fitted to E46 318d and 320d plus E39 520d. It uses 1,951 cc displacement, a Bosch VP44 rotary pump and a Garrett GT1549V turbo. It shares the family's timing chain and turbo issues but does not use swirl flaps, and it is not a straight swap with M47TU or M47TU2 because the fuel system, ECU and turbo plumbing differ.

2001-2004 Technical Update fitted to late E46 318d and 320d, early E60 520d and E83 X3 2.0d. Capacity increased to 1,995 cc and common-rail injection arrived, lifting output to 150 hp. This is the generation most exposed to swirl flap failure, and while it shares the block family with TU2, the turbo, ECU calibration and swirl flap design differ.

2004-2007 second Technical Update fitted to E87 118d and 120d, E90 318d and 320d, and later E60 520d. It keeps 1,995 cc and common-rail injection, adds a revised swirl flap design, and spans 122-163 hp outputs. It is generally the most robust M47 variant overall, although timing chain wear remains the primary concern.

variants.closing: How to confirm your code: the engine code is stamped on the block near the starter motor and may appear in service history, while the V5C confirms engine capacity rather than always showing the full suffix. buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement M47D20 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used M47D20 can make sense for lower-value E46 or E39 hosts, but only with documented service history and timing chain evidence. The biggest risk is inheriting an engine with a stretched chain or failing turbo - both are expensive to discover after purchase.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: For most owners this is the sweet spot. A proper M47D20 recon addresses the timing chain, tensioner, guides, turbo inspection and EGR cleaning, giving you a fresh engine with known-good critical components without the cost of a full rebuild.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for higher-value hosts such as late E90 or low-mileage examples, or where the original engine has sentimental or matching-numbers value. An upgraded rebuild should include a new oil pump chain, revised timing components and a swirl flap delete where appropriate.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All supply options can be fitted through our network of vetted UK BMW specialists with full warranty coverage nationwide. See supply and fit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The M47D20 typically sits in vehicles now worth around £1,500-£9,000, with many E46 320d examples below £3,000. If a reconditioned unit at £1,500-£2,200 exceeds roughly 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing. Late E90 and E87 examples with higher retained values more comfortably justify replacement.

related.title: Engines Related to the BMW M47D20

items.description: BMW's 1.7-litre turbo diesel that preceded the M47. The M41 was a 2-valve-per-cylinder unit; the M47 brought 16-valve technology and significantly more power.
The N47 replaced the M47 from 2007 onward. It delivered more power and efficiency, but introduced the infamous rear-mounted timing chain issues that have plagued BMW diesels ever since.
The transverse-mounted version of the M47D20 fitted to the Rover 75 and Land Rover Freelander. Same basic engine family, but different sump, mounts and ancillaries.
The 3.0-litre straight-six sibling to the M47. It shares the same broad architecture and many of the same failure patterns, but in a six-cylinder package.
The M47R variant was used in Freelander 1 models from 2000 to 2006. Same engine family, transverse configuration, different ancillaries and ECU mapping.
